folk.why:wayfinder: Moves into any room made ready for a holder.
folk.why:provisioner: Comes on word that one of us carries more coin than our hearths use.
folk.why:smith: Comes on word of an anvil. Whoever works iron will want harder ore.
folk.why:apothecary: Wants the fresh remains of Vanahar, and comes once it is dead.
folk.why:tinker: Has never seen a Joining Bench at work, and comes to ours.
folk.why:runescribe: A Line Frame brings this one. It means crystal out of the deep rock.
folk.why:beastcaller: Works with Tama remains, so comes once Kankāl is dead.
folk.why:deserter: Stays behind when a Sand March is beaten off at our walls.
folk.meet:wayfinder: You have a door, a light and a bed, peopl. I hold here from tonight.
folk.meet:provisioner: Word on the road is that you carry more lees than your hearths use, peopl. I carry goods. Buy or sell.
folk.meet:smith: An anvil means iron, peopl, and iron means you will dig for harder ore. I work metal.
folk.meet:apothecary: You killed Vanahar, peopl. I want its remains while they are fresh, and I sell salves.
folk.meet:tinker: So this is a joining bench, peopl. I have handled small pieces all my life and never seen two made one.
folk.meet:runescribe: A line frame, and crystal from the deep rock. I cut lines in stone, peopl, and a staff is the same work.
folk.meet:beastcaller: Kankāl is dead, peopl, so there will be Tama remains to be had at every dusk. That is my trade.
folk.meet:deserter: I came here with the march, peopl, and I stayed. I sell for Mūda and nothing else.
folk.housed:wayfinder: They said every stone on this road was lit once.
The crates at the next old houses are empty. Fill them if you pass that way.
I know where the stones of each kind lie. Ask me which one comes next.
Bedrolls come out of the old houses. No one born here has a use for one.
If you find a nest in a broken store by the road, clear it.
folk.housed:provisioner: I buy anything, because somebody two hearths on will want it.
Take food with you when you go Under.
Two pots this close bring them at dusk. I told the others so before I sat down here.
Every hearth on the road is short of something, and most are short of lees.
Bring me hide from Tusāravan. Beds on the road wear through it.
Coal sells in the cold country, if you have any to spare.
folk.housed:smith: Iron lifts with a stone pick. Hīrak needs iron.
I can shape a bar of any metal. Jalit and harder I cannot make.
A forge of remains against my wall draws, and I am the one sitting up beside it.
I have looked all my life for a forge of the forebears and never found a ring standing.
Bring me raw ore of a metal I have only seen poured.
If you get a tool whole out of a sealed store, let me see it before you use it.
folk.housed:apothecary: Put it on the table, away from the pot.
This is what a holder drinks at first light, and it does the same for your arm.
A second salve too soon does nothing. Wait.
An old holder's hand goes dead and sets, the way metal sets. The remains might loosen it.
It has not worked yet. I need more of the remains, and fresh.
Bring me any old salve you find in a sealed store.
folk.housed:tinker: The one who taught me had never joined two pieces either.
A second of the same adds nothing.
If you get into a sealed store, bring out the small things as well as the bars.
I can tell which store a piece came from by its make.
I know what a piece does by holding it.
Nobody makes pieces like these now. The skill went out of the hands.
folk.housed:runescribe: A staff is the same work as a hearthstone, pointed away from you.
A bad cut leaks into the arm.
Where to cut is learned by the hand. I cannot tell it to you.
I held one of those recall stones all night once, and it did nothing for me.
Crystal grows in the dark rock. There is nothing of any kill in it.
At a great stone, look at the place for the hand. Tell me how many lines leave it.
folk.housed:beastcaller: It stays for what is on the bone.
Do not bring it inside my walls. Unsalted is food, and I sit beside a pot.
If you find a nest in the old stonework, tell me what kind was in it before you break it.
A second one will stay for the whistle. They come to the sound.
The others do not like my trade. Food draws, they say.
Those eight at the stones are beasts, peopl. Big ones.
folk.housed:deserter: I marched with them and I will not again.
A Mūda is a night inside the light at any fire of ours.
While the burrower lived nothing else came up on the sand.
Everything I sell, a march took from a store and could not burn.
The old at the fires say another burrower will come onto the sand if the stones are left alone.
I know when a march will come and what it will go for.
folk.stage:wayfinder.1: Vanahar is dead, peopl. Its country is ours again, one step nearer every stone lit.
Kāru will come to a joining bench, and Vejja is already on the road for the remains.
folk.stage:wayfinder.2: Bed Maruhar's remains in a ring of Deep Rock, and the fire will melt Jalit.
folk.stage:wayfinder.3: They are saying on the road that Kankāl lay on a seal, and you have broken it.
The way Under is open to you now. Make the gate.
folk.stage:wayfinder.4: Guhamāt's remains in a ring of Hollow Rock will work Tala.
Jīmūt comes next. The kite is flown from its stone.
folk.stage:wayfinder.5: With Jīmūt dead, its remains make the second gate.
Where that gate goes, the telling does not say.
folk.stage:wayfinder.6: Work Patik in the furnace Ratan gives you, and make the mask for Kuranga from it.
folk.stage:wayfinder.7: Kuranga is dead. Gahan is yours now, and the key to the cairn is made of it.
folk.stage:wayfinder.8: You opened the cairn, peopl. The stones can be lit again.
Someone has to sit at one through the night. No one in any telling has.
folk.stage:provisioner.1: The remains of Vanahar are the best lees any pot on this road has had.
folk.stage:provisioner.2: A furnace made from Maruhar still burns coal, and I carry coal.
folk.stage:provisioner.3: So you broke a seal, the road says. Bad luck if so, and enough lees covers it.
folk.stage:provisioner.4: Caps from Under sell. Bring me some and I will find them a buyer.
folk.stage:provisioner.5: When you come back through the second gate, bring the fruit that grows there. I can sell it.
folk.stage:provisioner.6: I have never carried lees as strong as Ratan's.
folk.stage:provisioner.7: One left after Kuranga. Take food with you when you go for it.
folk.stage:provisioner.8: The cairn is open, they say. Lees is lees, and I will buy what you have.
folk.stage:smith.1: Vanahar had iron bars in it. I will take any you do not want.
folk.stage:smith.2: I can sell you Jalit now. I can work a bar of it, and I could never have made one.
Jalit heads come off the anvil holding the heat of the deep.
folk.stage:smith.3: Everyone on the road talks of a seal. All I know is that a gate frame is smith's work.
folk.stage:smith.4: Guhamāt's carcass was full of Antar. I have the bars to sell now.
folk.stage:smith.5: Jīmūt gave up Tala bars. Bring me the raw ore some day. I have only seen it as bars.
folk.stage:smith.6: Patik comes out of the Ratan Furnace. I can shape it once you have it.
folk.stage:smith.7: Gahan lies in the lowest rock, by what you say. I want to see a bar of it.
folk.stage:smith.8: The metal in the arms out of the cairn is better than mine. I want to see how it was worked.
folk.stage:apothecary.2: I still have some of the Vanahar remains. No dead hand has loosened yet.
folk.stage:apothecary.3: With Kankāl dead I can make the greater salve and the greater tonic, from what grows Under.
folk.stage:apothecary.4: Caps from Under make a broth that eases the arm. Bring me more of them.
folk.stage:apothecary.5: If anything grows past the second gate, bring me a piece of it.
folk.stage:apothecary.6: You come in cut after each of these, peopl. Sit, and let me look at you.
folk.stage:apothecary.7: Take salves with you for the last of them, peopl.
folk.stage:apothecary.8: Bring me a piece of what came out of the cairn, for the hands.
folk.stage:tinker.2: Kammār has Jalit now, so I can stock the Long Glove. There is a part of Jalit in it.
folk.stage:tinker.3: I would like to hold the plate that came off Kankāl, peopl.
folk.stage:tinker.4: Small ones form on Guhamāt's cap, I hear. Let me hold it.
folk.stage:tinker.5: Jīmūt's feather weighs almost nothing. Pieces of that stuff lie in the oldest stores.
folk.stage:tinker.6: That crystal of Ratan's is the best seat a line could have. Rehakār will say the same.
folk.stage:tinker.7: Let me hold that tine of Kuranga's before you wear it.
folk.stage:tinker.8: A gem in a piece of dressed stone came out of the cairn. Let me see it.
folk.stage:runescribe.1: You stood at a great stone. Count the lines that leave the place for the hand, and tell me.
folk.stage:runescribe.2: Did you count the lines on the stone in the sand? I want to know if it is the same cut.
folk.stage:runescribe.3: A seal, they are calling it. I have never cut one and would not know how.
folk.stage:runescribe.4: Guhamāt's stone is Under, where no born person will see its lines. Look at them for me.
folk.stage:runescribe.5: The second gate is a frame and remains, with no cut in it anywhere. I do not understand it.
folk.stage:runescribe.6: Ratan's crystal is the best seat a cut line can run to. Bring me a piece and I will cut to it.
folk.stage:runescribe.7: One stone left, peopl. The cairn is the first and best of them.
folk.stage:runescribe.8: The cairn is open, they say. Every stone lit again would need a hand on it, and it will not be mine.
folk.stage:beastcaller.4: They call Guhamāt mother. It was a beast that dropped food, and small ones formed on the food.
folk.stage:beastcaller.5: Jīmūt was a beast like the rest, only one that never landed.
folk.stage:beastcaller.6: Ratan was crystal with a beast inside it. I would have liked to see it eat.
folk.stage:beastcaller.7: Kuranga was the biggest of the pale beasts. That kind eats the other kinds.
folk.stage:beastcaller.8: Whatever was in the cairn, it was a beast. The others can call it what they like.
folk.stage:deserter.3: The dark night brings them up everywhere now. At the fires they will say the peopls did it.
folk.stage:deserter.4: Every kill you boil down is another store, peopl. Every store draws.
folk.stage:deserter.5: The flier's remains are in your gate now. A gate is a store, and it draws.
folk.stage:deserter.6: I do not know what you are killing now. Nobody at the fires does.
folk.stage:deserter.7: Another stone with nothing at it. The old at the fires say something comes to an empty stone.
folk.stage:deserter.8: At the fires they say that heap was closed over a thing nobody could kill. You killed it.
They will say it proves the stones breed them.
folk.night:wayfinder: My hand is on the stone until first light, peopl. Ask me about the road in the morning.
The goods are on the shelf. Leave the lees beside me.
folk.night:provisioner: I am holding. Take what you want and set the lees down by the pot.
Talk if you like. I cannot get up.
folk.night:smith: One hand is on the stone. The other can still take your lees.
Put a forge of remains against my wall and I am the one sitting up beside it.
folk.night:apothecary: My arm is on the stone. I will see to yours at first light.
A quiet night. The arm will only be sore.
folk.night:tinker: I cannot turn pieces over with one hand on the stone. Buy what you can see.
Come at first light and I will look at what you found.
folk.night:runescribe: The lines in this slab carry what my hand drives. I do not lift it until first light.
Ask me about cutting in the morning.
folk.night:beastcaller: Hand on the stone, peopl. Keep your small one out of this room.
Unsalted is food, and the dark is full of things that eat. Keep it away from my pot.
folk.night:deserter: I hold badly. It costs my arm more than it costs theirs.
I learned this by watching through walls I was sent to break.
folk.dark:wayfinder: Amāvassa. The moon is hollow tonight, and what was in it is on the ground.
Stay inside the light until the sun is up.
folk.dark:provisioner: No pack will come for the stores tonight. The things from the moon are out instead.
folk.dark:smith: The moon is dark. I have the door shut and my hand down hard.
folk.dark:apothecary: If you are hurt tonight, come in before you go out again.
folk.dark:tinker: I have never seen this many out under a dark moon.
folk.dark:runescribe: They say the moon is hollow tonight. Stay where there is light.
folk.dark:beastcaller: Those pale beasts eat the other kinds. Watch them do it, if you get the chance.
folk.dark:deserter: No one on the sand has seen a night like this.
Stay in the light, peopl. That is the one thing my people know to do.
folk.attack:wayfinder: They are at the walls. I do not fight, peopl. Keep them off the bed.
The pot does not turn what has come.
folk.attack:provisioner: They have come for the stores. Get between them and the chests.
I hold or I go. I do not fight.
folk.attack:smith: I have a hammer, and I still do not fight. That is your work.
Keep them off my anvil and off the bed.
folk.attack:apothecary: Stand at the edge, peopl. I am staying by the bed.
Bring me whoever is hurt when it is over.
folk.attack:tinker: They want what is in the chests. Do not let them have it.
I am not leaving the bed.
folk.attack:runescribe: No cut in any stone turns these. Fight them.
The edge is yours. I stay where I sit.
folk.attack:beastcaller: Kill them at the edge, peopl. I do not fight.
There will be remains for the bone when it is done.
folk.attack:deserter: Whatever is out there has come for what draws.
If it is a march, they will not stop for me. I left them.
folk.idle:wayfinder: Ask me where the next stone lies.
The crates down the road are empty.
I came a long road to sit at this one.
folk.idle:provisioner: Hide, meat, coal. I take all of it.
Somebody two hearths on is short of salt.
folk.idle:smith: Bring me ore I have not seen.
That edge wants a harder metal.
I work while it is light.
folk.idle:apothecary: Fresh remains, if you have them.
Come back when the salve has done its work.
folk.idle:tinker: Show me what you are wearing.
Two of the same do nothing for you.
folk.idle:runescribe: Have you stood at a great stone yet?
That crystal came out of deep rock.
folk.idle:beastcaller: Your small one is too near my pot.
Any nests where you have been?
It is the food it stays for.
folk.idle:deserter: The fires are a long walk from here.
folk.buy:wayfinder: That will see you down the road.
folk.buy:provisioner: That came three hearths to get here.
folk.buy:smith: My own make. It will hold.
folk.buy:apothecary: One at a time. A second too soon does nothing.
folk.buy:tinker: That one came out of an old store.
folk.buy:runescribe: That is cut true. It will not leak into your arm.
folk.buy:beastcaller: Keep the bone out of the house.
It forms on the food the first time you drive it.
folk.buy:deserter: A march took that out of a store like yours.
Mūda for it. That is the price.
folk.sell:wayfinder: Somebody down the road will want that.
folk.sell:provisioner: That goes on to the next hearth.
folk.sell:smith: I will take it for the metal.
folk.sell:apothecary: Fruit and caps go into the salves.
I will find a use for it.
folk.sell:tinker: I will turn it over and see what it does.
folk.sell:beastcaller: Remains go on the bone. Bring more.
folk.sell:deserter: I will sell it on to a walker.
folk.short:wayfinder: You are short. Nothing is lent on this road.
folk.short:provisioner: Not enough. Come back with the weight.
folk.short:smith: That does not cover it, and I lend nothing.
folk.short:apothecary: Short. Go and get the rest.
folk.short:tinker: You cannot pay that. Find a piece to sell me first.
folk.short:runescribe: Too little. I owe nobody and nobody owes me.
folk.short:beastcaller: There is not enough lees in that.
folk.short:deserter: Not enough Mūda. Beat off a march and you will have more.
folk.leave:wayfinder: You broke the bed, peopl. I will say why I left at the next hearth.
folk.leave:provisioner: The bed is gone, so I am. There are other roofs on the road.
folk.leave:smith: Without a bed there is no hearth here. I am taking my hammer down the road.
folk.leave:apothecary: I will sit down at some other house tonight.
folk.leave:tinker: No bed, so I go. I will think about that bench of yours.
folk.leave:runescribe: No bed, no seat for the night. I am leaving.
folk.leave:beastcaller: Broken. I take my bones and walk.
folk.leave:deserter: No bed. There is no fire for me either, so I will find another pot.
folk.extra:deserter.burrower: The burrower took our people for as long as we lived on its sand. You boiled them down with it.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_in: Amāvassa is in {n} nights, peopl. Be under a roof or where you mean to fight.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_in_one: Amāvassa is tomorrow night. Be inside the light by dusk.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_tonight: Amāvassa is tonight. The Chandasāvak are on the ground, and they carry the slivers.
walker.say:dusk: I sit at this well until dark, peopl. Then I take my pot into the nearest house and hold it.
The crate in the end house has food in it. Fill it again when you pass.
I walk by day and sit down wherever dusk finds me.
Two pots this close would bring a pack, so I am the only one here.
If you have a room with a bed and a light, there are holders on this road who would come to it.
My hand goes on the stone at dark. Ask me nothing after that.
walker.say:dark: Amāvassa, peopl. I am holding inside, and the door stays shut.
The moon is hollow tonight. Find a roof.
walker.say:raid: Packs are out for the stores tonight, and my pot is a store too.
Stand off from me, peopl. Whatever is after you will find my pot as well.
fire.say:before: Nothing comes up on this sand but the burrower's own, peopl. Do not bring a store onto it.
There is nothing here for you.
fire.say:after: You killed the burrower. The sand is open now.
Nothing of ours draws. Go back to your stores.
fire.say:night: Nothing comes up in this light. That is all it is for.
Stand where we can see you, and keep your hands off the fire.
fire.say:struck: Drive it out of the light. It will get up somewhere else.
You broke the fire's ground, peopl. We are on you until the next dawn.
fire.say:fuel: Wood. Leave it at the edge and go.
Coal burns longer. Set it down and step back.
The fire takes it. That buys you nothing.
march.say:march: Find the lees. It goes to the fire.
Cut the peopl down and go on. It gets up anyway.
Every store here draws. Burn it.
Back inside the light before dusk.
march.say:beaten: Drop what you carry and walk.
Dusk is coming. Back to the fire.
